description: PEACE LENS is building a tactile web app that uses NASA satellite data to show the everyday life armed conflict takes from a city, and to keep attention alive after the news moves on. From a globe split by the real sun, users descend into Mariupol, Gaza or Khartoum: NASA Black Marble shows lights going dark, FIRMS shows detected fires, HLS shows the streets that were there. We value honesty: same-season comparisons, ranges not single numbers, neutral wording, and what satellites cannot tell.
summary: PEACE LENS is a touch-driven web app that turns NASA Earth-observation time series into a trend you can feel: what happens to a city's lights when conflict arrives, and what happens after the news moves on. Start on a live globe — NASA Black Marble night lights, split by today's real sun — and descend into Mariupol, Gaza or Khartoum. Drag through 2022 night by night: Black Marble shows Mariupol going dark while NASA FIRMS shows where fire was detected (industrial heat seen before the war removed). One bar per October reveals the longer trend: the lights came back to about 90% of pre-war by 2025 — then fell to about 30% again in 2026, a drop confirmed by a second satellite (NOAA-20) while a control city stayed flat. Then trace your finger to turn tonight back into a pre-war October night. On a screen, one finger brings the lights back. Reality cannot be rewound. A daily job keeps watching the trend and sends a push alert when a city's lights change markedly.
details:
What it does. Eight short, hands-on scenes; nothing plays by itself.

1. Right now, on this planet — a globe with NASA Black Marble (median of 5 nights, Oct 2026) on the night side and Blue Marble on the day side, split by the real sun position. Red: 25,770 recorded events of organized violence in 60 countries in 2025 (UCDP — labelled "not satellite data").

2. Under each of these lights, someone was having dinner — the city's lights before the war.

3. There were schools — NASA HLS (30 m) daytime image with schools and kindergartens from OpenStreetMap.

4. The lights did not go out in a single night — drag through every valid night of Jan–Jul 2022 (Black Marble daily) while places where NASA FIRMS detected fire accumulate. Timeline marks open sourced records (OSCE/ODIHR, OHCHR, UN, ICRC) behind a content warning with a skip option.

5. Now — one bar per October, pre-war October = 100, with interquartile ranges. Mariupol: 34 (2022) → 75 → 88 → 92 (2025) → 32 (2026). Gaza 2026: 48; Khartoum 2026: 73 (each city's pre-war October = 100). "Satellites cannot tell why. We will not guess."

6. Rewind — trace tonight's dark city to reveal the same October before the war.

7. Your city — the area darker than pre-war in October 2026, at the same scale, draggable over Tokyo, Osaka, Sapporo, New York, Washington D.C. or London.

8. Until yesterday, life was ordinary here — type one thing you would protect and place it as a light in that darkness (kept on-device only). Keep watching: a PWA push alert when the trend changes.

Trend detection methods.

- Index = mean display brightness of NASA Black Marble (VNP46A2, daily, gap-filled, BRDF-corrected) over the city centre (Gaza: 1 km inside the official boundary to limit light bleeding). Median of October nights each year (n = 23–28 after removing no-data nights and nights identical to the previous one); interquartile range shown. Same-season comparison avoids snow/vegetation effects.

- The 2026 Mariupol drop began in late July 2026; NOAA-20's product shows the same drop, while the control city Rostov-on-Don stayed flat.

- Fires: before the invasion the city had 2,832 FIRMS detections on 127 days (steel plants). Places detected on ≥3 days in the six months before the war form three industrial zones that are excluded (45 of 297 detections); the remaining 252 are shown as places where fire was detected. No detection ≠ no fire (clouds, overpass times). Fires inside the zones are covered by the OSCE/ODIHR report.

- Darkened area = pixels whose brightness fell sharply between pre-war October and October 2026 (12–14-night medians), main connected area only, reported as a range over thresholds (~500 m pixels bloom, so areas look larger than the built-up city).

- Alerts: daily Cloud Scheduler job; median of the latest 14 valid nights ÷ the same pre-war month; alert when it moves ≥20 points from the last alert on two consecutive days, at most weekly. Stored: push endpoint + city key only. Data arrive about two weeks late.

What it cannot tell you. Night lights cannot distinguish outages, evacuation or destruction, and cannot assign cause or responsibility. Lights returning ≠ lives returning. Values are display-image brightness, not radiance, and the dark background is not subtracted.

Fairness. Every city uses one neutral template (date · event · parties). Individual records appear only where sourced; other cities say so.

Tools. Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, three.js, HTML Canvas + Pointer Events, Python (NumPy, Pillow, SciPy, Shapely), Node.js/Express, web-push, Google Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, Firestore.
